concept_definition: A perennial woody plant typically having a single main stem or trunk, supporting branches and leaves and growing to a considerable height.
the seed-bearing part of a flowering plant, consisting of reproductive structures (stamens and pistils) often surrounded by colorful petals
the green, often short plants with narrow leaves that grow widely on lawns and fields; the vegetation forming a turf
a flat, typically green plant organ attached to a stem or branch, where photosynthesis and gas exchange occur
a plot of ground, often near a house, used for growing flowers, vegetables, or ornamental plants; a planned outdoor area cultivated for aesthetic or productive purposes
an area of land, often owned by a city or public authority, set aside and maintained for public recreation, open space, and enjoyment (often with lawns, trees, paths, and playgrounds)
A type of tree known for its strength and durability, often producing acorns and used for timber.
A rose is a type of flowering plant known for its beautiful blooms and often sweet fragrance, commonly associated with love and beauty.
The part of a plant that typically grows underground, anchoring the plant and absorbing water and nutrients from the soil.
A woody limb that grows from the trunk or stem of a tree or shrub.
A small reproductive unit produced by a plant that can grow into a new plant.
The edible reproductive body of a seed plant, typically sweet or sour, eaten as food (singular, base form).
A large area covered chiefly with trees and undergrowth; a woodland ecosystem.
A wild plant that grows where it is not wanted, often among cultivated plants or in gardens.
The tough outer covering of a tree trunk and branches.
Fine powder produced by flowering plants that contains male reproductive cells and can fertilize other plants; often dispersed by wind or animals.
The main woody stem of a tree that supports branches and transports nutrients and water.
